guideTitle: The Best Budget Digital Notebooks for Digitizing Handwritten Notes
metaDescription: Under $30, a digital notebook means a reusable Rocketbook you scan with your phone. We compared seven by size, page style, binding and whether a pen is included.
introParagraphs: On a budget under $30, a digital notebook is a reusable paper notebook, not an electronic device. You write with an erasable pen, scan the pages with a phone app to send them to cloud services, then wipe the pages clean and start again. E Ink tablets and smart pens cost considerably more.

All seven picks here are Rocketbooks, so the decision is about format: pocket-size Mini, executive-size Flip, or letter-size Flip and Core, and whether the listing includes the pen. Rocketbook pages need a compatible erasable pen, so factor one in if it isn't included.
Prices ran from about $15 to $27 at the time of writing. Our comparison is based on listed sizes, page styles and included accessories, not hands-on testing.

rb-mini-black-budget.summary: A 3.5 x 5.5-inch Rocketbook Mini with dotted pages, the lowest price here.
rb-mini-black-budget.description:
The Rocketbook Mini is the least expensive way to try a reusable notebook: a pocket-size 3.5 x 5.5-inch notepad with dotted pages, about $15 at the time of writing.

Like every Rocketbook here, you scan pages with the app, then wipe them clean.

The small page suits lists and quick notes rather than meetings or lectures, and you'll need a compatible erasable pen if you don't have one.
rb-mini-black-budget.bestFor: Quick notes and lists on the move.
rb-mini-black-budget.skipIf: You take long notes; the letter-size Rocketbook Core gives far more space.

rb-mini-navy-budget.summary: The same Rocketbook Mini in navy blue, at the same price.
rb-mini-navy-budget.description:
This is the Rocketbook Mini in navy rather than black: the same 3.5 x 5.5-inch size, dotted pages and app scanning, at the same price at the time of writing.

Choose between them on color alone.

The same limits apply: a small page and a pen that may need buying separately.
pros: Same low price as the black Mini
rb-mini-navy-budget.bestFor: Readers who want the Mini in navy.
rb-mini-navy-budget.skipIf: Color doesn't matter; the black Mini is identical.

rb-flip-navy-budget.summary: A 6 x 8.8-inch Rocketbook Flip in navy, more room than the Mini.
rb-flip-navy-budget.description:
The executive-size Flip is the middle ground: 6 x 8.8 inches gives much more room than the Mini while staying portable, at about $25 at the time of writing.

It uses the same scan-and-wipe workflow.

The listing doesn't include a pen; the version with pen and cloth costs about $1 more.
rb-flip-navy-budget.bestFor: Meeting and daily notes in a bag-friendly size.
rb-flip-navy-budget.skipIf: You don't own a compatible pen; the Flip bundle includes one for about $1 more.

rb-flip-pen-budget.summary: An executive-size Flip with dotted and lined pages, plus pen and cleaning cloth.
rb-flip-pen-budget.description:
The Flip bundle is the complete starter kit: a 6 x 8.8-inch notepad with a mix of dotted and lined pages, plus a compatible pen and cleaning cloth, at about $26 at the time of writing.

That makes it the simplest way to start without buying anything else.

It is a notepad format rather than a full-size notebook.
cons: Costs slightly more than the plain Flip
rb-flip-pen-budget.bestFor: First-time users who want everything in one box.
rb-flip-pen-budget.skipIf: You already own a compatible pen; the plain navy Flip is slightly cheaper.

rb-flip-gray-budget.summary: An executive-size spiral-bound Rocketbook Flip in gray.
rb-flip-gray-budget.description:
This gray Flip is the executive-size spiral-bound notebook, about $26 at the time of writing, for readers who prefer a spiral binding.

It uses the same scan-and-wipe workflow as the others.

It costs the same as the Flip bundle but doesn't list a pen, so the bundle offers more for the money unless you want this color or binding.
cons: Same price as the pen bundle
rb-flip-gray-budget.bestFor: Readers who prefer a gray spiral notebook.
rb-flip-gray-budget.skipIf: You need a pen; the Flip bundle includes one at the same price.

rb-flip-graylet-budget.summary: A letter-size 8.5 x 11-inch Rocketbook Flip in gray, at about $25.
rb-flip-graylet-budget.description:
The letter-size Flip gives the most writing space for the money: 8.5 x 11 inches at about $25 at the time of writing, slightly less than the Rocketbook Core.

It suits lectures, long meetings and sketches.

It is bulkier than the executive and Mini formats, and a pen isn't listed.
rb-flip-graylet-budget.skipIf: You carry it daily; the executive Flip is more portable.

rb-core-budget.summary: Rocketbook's standard letter-size Core with dotted pages and a durable cover.
rb-core-budget.description:
The Rocketbook Core is the brand's standard notebook: letter-size, spiral-bound, with dotted pages and a durable cover, about $27 at the time of writing.

It is the most established model in the range, with the same app-connected scanning to cloud services.

It costs a little more than the letter-size Flip for similar space, and a pen isn't listed.
rb-core-budget.skipIf: You want the lowest letter-size price; the gray letter Flip costs slightly less.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Pick a size for how you write
buyingCriteria.explanation: Mini (3.5 x 5.5 in) for lists, executive (6 x 8.8 in) for daily notes, letter (8.5 x 11 in) for lectures and long meetings.
Rocketbook pages need a compatible erasable pen. Only the Flip bundle here lists one included.
Notes reach the cloud when you scan them with the app, not as you write.
Most here have dotted pages; the Flip bundle adds lined pages. Some are spiral-bound.

faq.q: Can I get an E Ink notebook under $30?
faq.a: Not among the options here. E Ink tablets cost considerably more; at this price, reusable paper notebooks are the realistic option.
Only the Flip bundle lists a pen. Rocketbook pages need a compatible erasable pen.
No. You scan each page with the Rocketbook app, which sends it to your chosen cloud service.
If you like writing by hand and want a digital copy, they're a low-cost way to do both, and the pages can be wiped and reused.

bottomLine: If you're new to reusable notebooks, the Flip bundle is the easiest start because it includes the pen. For the lowest cost, the Rocketbook Mini covers quick notes.

For more space, the letter-size Flip is slightly cheaper than the Core, while the Core is the established standard. Several picks here differ only by color, so buy whichever format fits and is cheapest when you shop.
